result.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
result.summary: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain. Code and data will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ReactBench-AD 驾驶基准：在真实 NAVSIM 与 PhysicalAI 场景中，跨全部相机视角与历史帧一致地合成横穿行人、静止行人和静止车辆，形成像素级反事实对照，评估四个 VLA 与两个 WAM 对路径上突发物体的反应，并通过短微调检验该反应能否被教出。
AI.relevance_reason: 像素级反事实对可隔离视觉证据对输出轨迹的因果作用，为核查「答案是否真正使用视觉内容」及视觉旁路、信息坍缩提供可借鉴的评价范式；其反应微弱的结果也可供核查多模态模型是否忽略任务必要的视觉细节。
